passages.text: David, however, said to himself, “One of these days now I will be swept away by the hand of Saul. There is nothing better for me than to escape to the land of the Philistines. Then Saul will stop searching for me all over Israel, and I will slip out of his hand.”
passages.sermon:
David was a man chosen by God.
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul wanted to kill David.
David spoke to himself.
He said, “One day Saul will catch me.
He will kill me.
I must escape.
The best way is to go to the land of the Philistines.
If I go there, Saul will stop looking for me in Israel.
Then I will escape from Saul.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר דָּוִד֙ אֶל־ לִבּ֔וֹ עַתָּ֛ה אֶסָּפֶ֥ה יוֹם־ אֶחָ֖ד בְּיַד־ שָׁא֑וּל אֵֽין־ לִ֨י ט֜וֹב כִּ֣י הִמָּלֵ֥ט אִמָּלֵ֣ט׀ אֶל־ אֶ֣רֶץ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֗ים וְנוֹאַ֨שׁ מִמֶּ֤נִּי שָׁאוּל֙ לְבַקְשֵׁ֤נִי עוֹד֙ בְּכָל־ גְּב֣וּל יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְנִמְלַטְתִּ֖י מִיָּדֽוֹ׃

passages.text: So David set out with his six hundred men and went to Achish son of Maoch, the king of Gath.
passages.sermon:
David was a leader in Israel.
David decided to leave Israel.
David took six hundred men with him.
These men were loyal to David.
David and his men traveled together.
They went to Achish.
Achish was the son of Maoch.
Achish was the king of Gath.
passages.original: וַיָּ֣קָם דָּוִ֔ד וַיַּעֲבֹ֣ר ה֔וּא וְשֵׁשׁ־ מֵא֥וֹת אִ֖ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עִמּ֑וֹ אֶל־ אָכִ֥ישׁ בֶּן־ מָע֖וֹךְ מֶ֥לֶךְ גַּֽת׃

passages.text: David and his men settled in Gath with Achish. Each man had his family with him, and David had his two wives: Ahinoam of Jezreel and Abigail of Carmel, the widow of Nabal.
passages.sermon:
David was a leader.
David had men who followed him.
David and his men went to Gath.
Achish was the king of Gath.
David and his men stayed with Achish in Gath.
Each man brought his family.
David had two wives.
One wife was Ahinoam from Jezreel.
The other wife was Abigail from Carmel.
Abigail had been the wife of Nabal.
passages.original: וַיֵּשֶׁב֩ דָּוִ֨ד עִם־ אָכִ֥ישׁ בְּגַ֛ת ה֥וּא וַאֲנָשָׁ֖יו אִ֣ישׁ וּבֵית֑וֹ דָּוִד֙ וּשְׁתֵּ֣י נָשָׁ֔יו אֲחִינֹ֙עַם֙ הַיִּזְרְעֵאלִ֔ית וַאֲבִיגַ֥יִל אֵֽשֶׁת־ נָבָ֖ל הַֽכַּרְמְלִֽית׃

passages.text: And when Saul learned that David had fled to Gath, he no longer searched for him.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
David was his former servant and rival.
Someone told Saul that David had fled to Gath.
Gath was a Philistine city.
After Saul heard this news, he stopped searching for David.
passages.original: וַיֻּגַּ֣ד לְשָׁא֔וּל כִּֽי־ בָרַ֥ח דָּוִ֖ד גַּ֑ת וְלֹֽא־ יוֹסַף ע֖וֹד לְבַקְשֽׁוֹ׃ס

passages.text: Then David said to Achish, “If I have found favor in your eyes, let me be assigned a place in one of the outlying towns, so I can live there. For why should your servant live in the royal city with you?”
passages.sermon:
David was a leader of men.
Achish was the king of Gath.
David spoke to Achish.
David said, “If I have found favor in your eyes, let me have a place in one of the country towns.
Let me live there.
Why should your servant live in the royal city with you?”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֜ד אֶל־ אָכִ֗ישׁ אִם־ נָא֩ מָצָ֨אתִי חֵ֤ן בְּעֵינֶ֙יךָ֙ יִתְּנוּ־ לִ֣י מָק֗וֹם בְּאַחַ֛ת עָרֵ֥י הַשָּׂדֶ֖ה וְאֵ֣שְׁבָה שָּׁ֑ם וְלָ֨מָּה יֵשֵׁ֧ב עַבְדְּךָ֛ בְּעִ֥יר הַמַּמְלָכָ֖ה עִמָּֽךְ׃

passages.text: That day Achish gave him Ziklag, and to this day it still belongs to the kings of Judah.
passages.sermon:
Achish was the king of Gath.
David was a servant of Achish.
On that day, Achish gave Ziklag to David.
Ziklag became the property of the kings of Judah.
Ziklag still belongs to the kings of Judah today.
passages.original: וַיִּתֶּן־ ל֥וֹ אָכִ֛ישׁ בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא אֶת־ צִֽקְלָ֑ג לָכֵ֞ן הָיְתָ֤ה צִֽקְלַג֙ לְמַלְכֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃פ

passages.text: And the time that David lived in Philistine territory amounted to a year and four months.
passages.sermon:
David was a leader of Israel.
David lived in Philistine territory.
He stayed there for one year.
He also stayed there for four months.
passages.original: וַֽיְהִי֙ מִסְפַּ֣ר הַיָּמִ֔ים אֲשֶׁר־ יָשַׁ֥ב דָּוִ֖ד בִּשְׂדֵ֣ה פְלִשְׁתִּ֑ים יָמִ֖ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֥ה חֳדָשִֽׁים׃

passages.text: Now David and his men went up and raided the Geshurites, the Girzites, and the Amalekites. (From ancient times these people had inhabited the land extending to Shur and Egypt.)
passages.sermon:
David was the leader of his men.
David and his men went up from their place.
They attacked the Geshurites.
They attacked the Girzites.
They attacked the Amalekites.
The Geshurites, Girzites, and Amalekites lived in that land for a long time.
They had lived there since ancient times.
Their land stretched from Shur to the border of Egypt.
passages.original: וַיַּ֤עַל דָּוִד֙ וַֽאֲנָשָׁ֔יו וַֽיִּפְשְׁט֛וּ אֶל־ הַגְּשׁוּרִ֥י וְהַגִּרְזִי וְהָעֲמָלֵקִ֑י כִּ֣י הֵ֜נָּה יֹשְׁב֤וֹת הָאָ֙רֶץ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר מֵֽעוֹלָ֔ם בּוֹאֲךָ֥ שׁ֖וּרָה וְעַד־ אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: Whenever David attacked a territory, he did not leave a man or woman alive, but he took the flocks and herds, the donkeys, camels, and clothing. Then he would return to Achish, who would ask him, “What have you raided today?” And David would reply, “The Negev of Judah,” or “The Negev of Jerahmeel,” or “The Negev of the Kenites.”
passages.sermon:
David was the leader of his men.
David attacked a territory.
David did not leave any man alive.
David did not leave any woman alive.
David took the flocks.
David took the herds.
David took the donkeys.
David took the camels.
David took the clothing.
David returned to Achish.
Achish was the Philistine ruler.
Achish asked David, “What have you raided today?”
David answered Achish.
David said, “The Negev of Judah.”
David also said, “The Negev of Jerahmeel.”
David also said, “The Negev of the Kenites.”
passages.original: וְהִכָּ֤ה דָוִד֙ אֶת־ הָאָ֔רֶץ וְלֹ֥א יְחַיֶּ֖ה אִ֣ישׁ וְאִשָּׁ֑ה וְלָקַח֩ צֹ֨אן וּבָקָ֜ר וַחֲמֹרִ֤ים וּגְמַלִּים֙ וּבְגָדִ֔ים וַיָּ֖שָׁב וַיָּבֹ֥א אֶל־ אָכִֽישׁ׃ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אָכִ֔ישׁ אַל־ פְּשַׁטְתֶּ֖ם הַיּ֑וֹם וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֗ד עַל־ נֶ֤גֶב יְהוּדָה֙ וְעַל־ נֶ֣גֶב הַיַּרְחְמְאֵלִ֔י וְאֶל־ נֶ֖גֶב הַקֵּינִֽי׃

passages.text: David did not leave a man or woman alive to be brought to Gath, for he said, “Otherwise they will report us, saying, ‘This is what David did.’ ” And this was David’s custom the whole time he lived in Philistine territory.
passages.sermon:
David was the leader of his men.
David lived in Philistine territory.
David attacked the people of the land.
David did not leave any man alive.
David did not leave any woman alive.
David did not bring any survivors to Gath.
David said, “Otherwise they will report us.”
He said, “They will say, ‘This is what David did.’”
David did this every time he attacked.
David kept this custom the whole time he lived among the Philistines.
passages.original: וְאִ֨ישׁ וְאִשָּׁ֜ה לֹֽא־ יְחַיֶּ֣ה דָוִ֗ד לְהָבִ֥יא גַת֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר פֶּן־ יַגִּ֥דוּ עָלֵ֖ינוּ לֵאמֹ֑ר כֹּֽה־ עָשָׂ֤ה דָוִד֙ וְכֹ֣ה מִשְׁפָּט֔וֹ כָּל־ הַ֨יָּמִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָשַׁ֖ב בִּשְׂדֵ֥ה פְלִשְׁתִּֽים׃

passages.text: So Achish trusted David, thinking, “Since he has made himself an utter stench to his people Israel, he will be my servant forever.”
passages.sermon:
Achish was a Philistine ruler.
David was an Israelite who lived among the Philistines.
Achish trusted David.
Achish thought David had made himself hated by his own people, Israel.
Achish believed David could never return to Israel.
Achish said, “David has become a stench to his people Israel.”
Achish decided, “David will be my servant forever.”
passages.original: וַיַּאֲמֵ֥ן אָכִ֖ישׁ בְּדָוִ֣ד לֵאמֹ֑ר הַבְאֵ֤שׁ הִבְאִישׁ֙ בְּעַמּ֣וֹ בְיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְהָ֥יָה לִ֖י לְעֶ֥בֶד עוֹלָֽם׃פ
